text: The wise woman builds her house, but the foolish one tears hers down with her own hands.
Whoever walks uprightly fears the LORD, but the one whose ways are crooked despises him.
In the mouth of a fool is a rod of pride, but the lips of the wise protect them.

versions.text: In the mouth of a fool is a rod for his own back, but the lips of the wise protect them.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "a rod (or shoot) of pride." The rendering "for his own back" supplies words not present in the text and drops the key term "pride," which is the point of the proverb — the fool's proud speech is what brings punishment.

text: Where there are no oxen, the manger is clean, but a strong ox brings an abundant harvest.
A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.

versions.text: A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out deceit.
versions.explanation: כְּזָבִים means "lies/falsehoods," not "deceit" (מִרְמָה, which appears in v. 25). Keeping the terms distinct preserves the wording of both proverbs.

versions.text: A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness pours out falsehood.
versions.explanation: כְּזָבִים is plural ("lies"), and the plain word "lies" echoes the verb "does not lie" in the first line, tightening the contrast and giving a crisper cadence for reading aloud. "Falsehood" is accurate but abstract and singular where the Hebrew is concrete and plural.

text: The mocker searches for wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
Keep away from a fool, for you will find no knowledge on his lips.
The wisdom of the prudent is to understand their way, but the folly of fools is deception.
Fools mock at guilt, but among the upright there is favor.
The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares its joy.
The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
There is a way that seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.
Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy can end in grief.
The faithless heart will be filled with the fruit of its own ways, and the good man with the fruit of his.
The gullible believe anything, but the prudent watch their steps.
The wise are cautious and turn away from evil, but the fool rushes ahead in reckless confidence.

versions.text: The wise fear the LORD and turn from evil, but the fool rushes ahead in reckless confidence.
versions.explanation: The divine name is not present in this verse; the Hebrew simply says the wise "fears and turns from evil." Adding "the LORD" inserts content not in the text (unlike vv. 26–27, where the name does appear).

text: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, and a scheming man is hated.
The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
The evil will bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
The poor are shunned even by their neighbors, but the rich have many friends.
Whoever despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is the one who is kind to the needy.
Do not those who plot evil go astray? But love and faithfulness belong to those who plan what is good.
All hard work brings profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
The crown of the wise is their wealth, but the folly of fools yields only folly.
A truthful witness saves lives, but the one who breathes out lies is treacherous.
In the fear of the LORD there is a strong refuge; it will be a shelter for his children.
The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a person away from the snares of death.
A large population is a king's glory, but without subjects a prince is ruined.
Whoever is patient shows great understanding, but a quick-tempered man displays folly.
A tranquil heart gives life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
Whoever oppresses the poor insults their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors him.
The wicked are brought down by their own evil, but the righteous find refuge even in death.
Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning, but among fools it makes itself known.
Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
A king delights in a servant who is wise, but his wrath falls on the one who brings shame.
